clue.text: Male cracks a whopper, reminding one of builder's butt!

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the low-slung trousers themselves

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a buster is something unusually large, a whopper
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man telling a tall tale while flashing the top of his backside like a workman bending over.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSTER takes M inside. 'Builder's butt' is the exposed top of the buttocks above sagging trousers, which these deliberately low-cut trousers imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumsters are trousers cut so low on the hips that they show the cleft of the buttocks, the fashion version of a workman's exposure.

clue.text: Culmination of sumo follows major blow in this?

definitions.text: Culmination of sumo follows major blow in this?

indicators.note: a culmination is the final point, so only the closing letter of the word is wanted
follows says the second piece comes after the first in the answer

blocks.note: a bash is a heavy blow
the final letter of sumo

explanation.surface: A sumo bout ends with a mighty shove, and the question asks where that happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a sumo tournament is just where a big blow finishes off a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A basho is an official Japanese sumo tournament, the event in which such decisive blows are struck.

clue.text: Below middle of tum he's portly but after training becomes trim

indicators.note: only the central letter of the following word is taken
training reshapes something, so these letters are put through a rearrangement
in a down entry, a piece set below another is written after it

blocks.note: the centre letter of tum
the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A paunchy man gets slim after a fitness regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like the slimmed-down result of training; here it is the noun for a car's interior finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim is the interior fittings and coverings of a vehicle, which is its upholstery.

clue.text: I'll join Laplanders in workers' organization

indicators.note: 'll is will, and will join means this piece attaches onto the end of the other

blocks.note: Chambers lists Samit as a form of Sami, the people of Lapland
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will throw in their lot with the Lapps in a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll' is read as 'I will', so I joins on the end of the Lapp people's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Samiti is an Indian term for an association or committee, such as a workers' union.

clue.text: Row of old guns producing broadside

blocks.note: first meaning: an obsolete word for a tier of guns on a ship
second meaning: the discharge of all those guns together

explanation.surface: A line of antique cannon on a warship lets fly a full salvo.
explanation.definitionFit: In old naval usage a tire is a tier of guns and also the simultaneous firing of them, a broadside.

clue.text: Outrage caused by soldiers in the course of hostility

indicators.note: something happening in the course of something else sits inside it

blocks.note: enmity is hostility
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An atrocity committed by troops during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a grave crime or monstrous wrong, an outrage.

clue.text: Erstwhile conductor in bus mostly with lot transported

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes
transported means carried off elsewhere, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before its last letter is dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bus conductor of the past riding along with a crowd being carried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests the man collecting fares on a bus; it is an orchestral conductor. The shortened bus and lot are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Adrian Boult was a leading British orchestral conductor of the twentieth century, now dead.

clue.text: Good queen about king 'I smother with affection'

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the others

blocks.note: Good Queen Bess was the popular name for Elizabeth I
K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kindly queen speaks of her king, declaring she smothers him with love.
explanation.walkthrough: BESS goes around K and I together.
explanation.definitionFit: To bekiss is an old word meaning to cover someone with kisses, to overwhelm with affection.

clue.text: Antelope as beast of burden going round tracks?

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: an ox is a draught animal
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: An antelope used for carrying loads, plodding around its trails.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large African and Arabian antelope with long straight horns.

clue.text: A gun going off, 'umongous start of destruction without measure?

indicators.note: something going off has gone wrong or exploded, so these letters fly into a new order
only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
huge with its H dropped, as the apostrophe in the clue signals
the opening letter of destruction

explanation.surface: A weapon fires, causing huge devastation beyond reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Umongous is humongous said with a dropped H, so it stands for 'uge, an aitch-less huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungauged means not measured, so something is literally without a measurement taken.

clue.text: 'E's sluggish, needing to be got up for a bit of a dance

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: he's with the H dropped
inert means sluggish

explanation.surface: A lazy fellow has to be roused to join in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase ES INERT is read upwards in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The trénise is one figure of the quadrille, so only a part of that whole dance.

clue.text: Legal sponsor representing oneself (without son) occupying large house

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters for son are removed
to occupy a place is to be inside it

blocks.note: a manor is a large country house
doing something in person means representing oneself

explanation.surface: A lawyer acting for himself, minus his son, living in a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representing oneself' sounds like a litigant without counsel, but it is a phrase meaning in one's own body; a mainpernor is a term from medieval English law.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainpernor was a surety in old English law who guaranteed a prisoner's appearance in court, a legal sponsor.

clue.text: Arm waving in group of sheaves, a national emblem

indicators.note: something waving moves about, so the letters are rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a shock is a stack of sheaves of corn
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone waves an arm amid the harvest stooks, a picture of rural national pride.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock, a three-leaved clover, is the emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: I rent denim, changing? Changing for this is now rare!

definitions.text: Changing for this is now rare!

indicators.note: the first changing tells us the words just before it alter their letter order

blocks.note: the ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hires jeans to wear, noting that dressing up for the evening meal hardly happens now.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the trick: the first is the anagram signal, the second is dressing up, which few now bother to do for the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing into formal clothes before the evening meal was once usual and is now uncommon, so this describes the meal hour cryptically.

clue.text: Part of edible catch all right in belly of ship

indicators.note: a belly is the middle part of a body, so the central letters are kept
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the two central letters of ship
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Some of the fish is stowed safely in the hold of a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoki is a New Zealand food fish, so one species in a catch of edible fish.

clue.text: Verse I name after alliance, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
after says the later pieces follow the first

blocks.note: the Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan, read backwards
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A poet names an alliance in a reflective verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixain is a stanza of six lines, a unit of verse.

clue.text: Sweet gin loom spinning with ends of thread

indicators.note: spinning turns things round and round, so the letters are jumbled
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of thread

explanation.surface: A weaving loom whirs with cotton thread, oddly mentioned beside a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: All of LOOM plus the two thread ends make the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Tom is a sweetened style of gin popular in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Rage when heading north entering Scots border, attracting tax

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from the bottom up
entering means going inside

blocks.note: dule is a Scots word for a boundary mark
bait is British slang for a fit of temper, read upwards

explanation.surface: Fury crossing the Scottish frontier, as if smuggled goods were taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang someone 'in a bait' is in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutiable goods are liable to customs duty, so they attract tax.

clue.text: Organ, or rag, distributing the written word?

indicators.note: distributing means spreading something apart, so one piece is split by another

blocks.note: prose is ordinary written language
tat is a rag or shabby material

explanation.surface: A newspaper, or rag, spreading the printed word: an organ of the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'rag' both suggest newspapers; the definition is a gland in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The prostate is a gland of the male reproductive system, an organ of the body.

clue.text: Antelope inhabiting the States, east to west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going east to west means reading right to left

blocks.note: inhabiting a place is being in it
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An antelope living in America, ranging from coast to coast.
explanation.walkthrough: IN US is read backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The suni is a small East African antelope.

clue.text: Energy-filled hospital facilities? Armies will want their support (7, two words)

indicators.note: filled means something has been put inside

blocks.note: wards are hospital rooms
go is energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Wards brimming with energy, which military forces will rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: armies have always prayed for backing from these deities.
explanation.definitionFit: Deities of battle, like Mars or Ares, are the gods an army would hope to have on its side.

clue.text: Three out of twelve growing wild in grass I planted (8, two words)

indicators.note: plants growing wild spread in no order, so these letters are jumbled
something planted is set into something else

blocks.note: the seven letters rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Three of twelve plants run wild in the lawn someone has sown.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides a number puzzle: the twelve are the signs of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, Libra and Aquarius are the zodiac's air signs, three of its twelve signs.

clue.text: Site of famous tablet found round Troy? It's been turned over, I swear

definitions.note: the words an attestor says, standing for the person

indicators.note: found round means surrounding
turned over means flipped end to end, so the whole is read backwards

t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system

explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' looks like the ancient city; it is the troy weight abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestor bears witness by solemn declaration, so the phrase 'I swear' is what one says.

clue.text: Scale as in wee round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the second word encloses the first

blocks.note: sma is Scots for small, wee
qua means as, in the capacity of

explanation.walkthrough: Sma is the Scots word for small, the same register as wee.
explanation.definitionFit: A squama is a scale, as on a fish or reptile or of skin, from the Latin word.

clue.text: Orangey stuff, one to get (but not in)

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letters named are dropped

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, one
to attain is to get

explanation.surface: Somebody offered orange dye is told to fetch it but stay outside.
explanation.walkthrough: ATTAIN loses IN to leave ATTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatta, also annatto, is an orange-red dye from a tropical tree, used to colour cheese and butter.

clue.text: English out of place in current plundering of Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: Only the E in RIFE moves, from last place to second.
explanation.definitionFit: Reif is a Scots word for robbery or plunder, so it is plundering as said in Scotland.

clue.text: Timber tree? Various cut with head of axe

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the final letter is lopped off

blocks.note: sundry means various, with its last letter cut
the opening letter of axe

explanation.surface: Assorted trees felled by an axe for wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundra, or sundri, is an Indian mangrove tree valued for its hard timber.

clue.text: Lofty stronghold that is taking a year to subdue it

explanation.walkthrough: To subdue something is to keep it under; in a down entry, IE sits below the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrie is a variant of eyrie, an eagle's high nest, by extension a lofty fortress.

clue.text: Train guard's aid in determining quantities?

indicators.note: to train something is to shape it, so these letters are reformed

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train guard' reads as a railway worker; 'quantities' means the length of syllables in verse.

clue.text: Take a little girl climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: bird is British slang for a young woman

explanation.definitionFit: To drib is an old verb meaning to cut off or take away small amounts at a time.

clue.text: Dog having special identification mark

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for special
a tag is a label that identifies

explanation.surface: A dog wearing its name tag on a collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stag someone is to shadow or spy on them, just as to dog someone is to follow them.

clue.text: Virtuosic person (if lacking that prime bit of prowess)?

definitions.text: Virtuosic person (if lacking that prime bit of prowess)?

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the named letter is removed
the prime bit is the first, so only the opening letter is meant

blocks.note: party is a facetious or legal word for a person

clue.text: Tot I disposed of in an appropriate place? Lots'll be disposed of here

in places one piece inside the other

clue.text: Fix the bounds for title aimed for distribution

clue.text: Heir, on being given bit with end of estate

the final letter of estate
